content:
My 6.5-year journey with #VisionIAS ended in 2020, during the #COVID-19 pandemic. Yet some memories remain close to my heart.
I remember calling Ajay sir about my pending payment. Around 20 of my classes were still left across two ongoing batches, which were covered by giving students access to recordings from earlier batches. When I requested the money, he transferred it immediately. I still remember that gesture with gratitude.
Today, hearing reports of delayed staff salaries and students boycotting the institute is deeply painful. For me, #VisionIAS will always be a place where I spent an important part of my teaching life, formed relationships and shared a dream.
In our meetings, Ajay sir would often say, “We want to be number one in the field.” There was conviction in those words, and at one point, that dream felt so close.
I don’t know what went wrong. People I am still in touch with offer different explanations, but I would rather not speculate about matters I don’t fully understand.
What I do know is that #Vision IAS was once a place where so many #teachers aspired to work. It is difficult to see an institution you helped build, even in a small way, go through such a phase.
I sincerely hope it finds its footing again—for its students, its staff, and everyone who gave years of their life to it.
